justification: Two speed fixes to the daily DCP read: stop re-reading a chapter refused twice on an unchanged PDF, and read two chapters at once in review mode

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_extract_parallel_and_hold.py (Linux) and tests/test_extract_refusal_db.py (CI isolated DB)
falsifiable_check.fails_when: a chapter refused twice on the same hash is still selected, a credit failure counts as a refusal, results come back out of order, or a dead worker drops its chapters
falsifiable_check.observed_red: first Linux run: 2 errors where the conftest psycopg2 stub had no connect; first Windows run: the crash test hit the sequential path and raised, so it was made fork-only

pre_impl.existing_data: no table records extraction outcomes; canterbury_bankstown chapter-7-6 refused 4 times on 2026-11-03 on one content hash
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: threads looked simplest, but extract_pdf_isolated forks and its comment relies on there being no threads, so workers are processes
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: three registry columns, a NOT condition in the existing selection builder, and the existing per-chapter loop moved into run_chapters

functions.name: run_chapters
functions.input: the selected chapters, the S3 client and connection, CLI args and an S3 client factory
functions.output: one (ok, review_data) per chapter in the chapters' order
functions.if_none: a worker that dies leaves its chapters reported as (False, None) and printed, never dropped

functions.name: is_content_refusal
functions.input: the error string returned by the isolated PDF work
functions.output: True only for PageLoss or ChunkLoss
functions.if_none: None or an empty error is False, so it never counts toward a hold

break_it.scenario: the OpenAI account runs out of credit twice on a chapter that only needs a retry
break_it.what_happens: the chapter would be held as if its PDF were broken

break_it.scenario: a chapter's content hash is NULL
break_it.what_happens: NOT(NULL = NULL AND ...) is NULL and the chapter would silently never be read
break_it.how: coalesce(... , false) and a DB test refusing a no-hash chapter three times

break_it.scenario: the chapter-7-6 worker is killed by Railway for memory halfway through a review run
break_it.what_happens: its chapters could vanish from the summary and look like nothing was flagged
break_it.how: missing results are printed and returned as failed

break_it.scenario: two chapters read at once double the peak memory of the PDF children
break_it.what_happens: Railway could kill a child for memory, which the extractor reports as a failed chapter
break_it.how: DCP_EXTRACT_PARALLEL=1 restores one at a time; measured peak was 726 MB for one chapter
break_it.repro: set DCP_EXTRACT_PARALLEL=1 on the dcp-extract service

break_it.scenario: a chapter is held after two refusals and the council never changes the PDF
break_it.what_happens: the chapter would never be read again and keep serving the previous edition
break_it.how: Sol review: the hold lasts 7 days from the last refusal, then one more try; the watchdog 48h alarm shows it meanwhile

break_it.scenario: worker A finishes chapter k0 then is killed on chapter k2 before its queue thread flushed
break_it.what_happens: k0's finished review read was lost and reported as failed
break_it.how: measured on Linux; each worker now sends on its own pipe and send() completes before the next chapter

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - apply migration 122 to production BEFORE merging (the new selection reads its columns), then check the next run prints [held] for chapter-7-6 after its second refusal and reads 2 chapters at once
